1b4ceca6cc6589f8c2b4b1afd0d7e6b5d0b21aed.summary: South Korea's National Cyber Security Center (NCSC) attributes 2024 supply chain attacks on South Korean organisations to North Korean groups Kimsuky (APT43) and Andariel (APT45). Kimsuky used a compromised construction trade website to distribute trojanized security installers signed with a valid certificate. Andariel abused a flaw in a domestic VPN's update process to push fake updates installing the DoraRAT remote access trojan at construction and machinery firms. The advisory believes the aim is trade-secret theft.

1bf4bcdf9454d3419317ee46ff1c57c642beb3df.summary: Malpedia family page for GandCrab, a ransomware-as-a-service that emerged in January 2018 and spread widely through affiliates. Its operators announced an end to operations on May 31, 2019, citing large profits, and the page notes they might resurface. The page is mostly a list of vendor reporting, covering links to REvil, a Vidar infostealer combination, and a 2020 arrest of an operator in Belarus.

1b9a9fd865cc671ceef94c0ddcfbe8bb99fdc182.summary: Trend Micro describes a small VPS hosting provider with servers in the Netherlands and Romania, formally registered in Dubai, that it says was used for over 100 serious cyber attacks since May 2015. Pawn Storm used its servers for at least 80 attacks against governments, and DustySky also used it. The provider also hosted a Carbanak C&C server and had the bulletproof host Maxided as a customer. The report describes short-lived BGP routing announcements that appear to obscure malicious activity. The owner's identity is unclear.
